tender.title: Recreation Ground Pavilion Upgrade of Toilets, Showers and Hot Water System
tender.description: The successful contractor shall provide all labour, materials, plant, equipment, supervision, and waste disposal necessary to complete the works described below. Plumbing and Hot Water Systems •	Remove and responsibly dispose of the existing hot water cylinder. •	Supply and install a new energy-efficient hot water system suitable for the building's intended use and occupancy levels. •	All plumbing works shall comply with current Building Regulations and Water Regulations. •	Contractor to recommend and specify the most appropriate replacement system within their tender submission. Shower Facilities •	Remove all existing shower installations. •	Supply and install individual showers within separate shower cubicles. •	Complete all associated plumbing, drainage and electrical works. •	Ensure adequate ventilation is maintained or upgraded as required. Toilet Refurbishment •	Remove all existing sanitaryware and associated fittings. •	Supply and install new WC suites, wash hand basins, taps and accessories. •	Layout shall follow the design and arrangement shown on the drawings supplied by the Council. •	Include necessary alterations to drainage, water supply and waste connections. •	All facilities must comply with current accessibility requirements where applicable. Entrance Area Alterations •	Carefully demolish and remove internal partition walls within the entrance area as indicated on the drawings. •	Create an open-plan social area. •	Make good all affected surfaces including ceilings, walls and floors. •	Undertake any necessary structural works identified during the contractor's investigations. •	Contractor shall verify wall construction prior to commencement and provide any required structural calculations. Flooring Works •	Remove existing floor finishes within all shower, toilet and bathroom areas. •	Prepare subfloors as required. •	Supply and install new slip-resistant commercial-grade flooring suitable for wet environments. •	All junctions, trims and finishes to be completed to a professional standard. Wall Coverings •	Remove existing wall tiles where necessary. •	Prepare wall surfaces. •	Supply and install new wall coverings, as recommended by the contractor, whether that be tile or shower panels within shower and bathroom areas. Wall coverings to be provided by the contractor but chosen by the Council. •	Ensure that all shower areas have trims and sealants where required. •	All finishes to be durable, easy to clean and suitable for heavy public use. Contractor Requirements The contractor shall: •	Undertake a site visit prior to tender submission. •	Provide a detailed programme of works. •	Minimise disruption to users of the recreation ground. •	Maintain safe access to the site at all times. •	Be responsible for all site health and safety arrangements. •	Provide evidence of relevant insurances including:  o	Public Liability Insurance (£10 million minimum). o	Employers' Liability Insurance (£10 million minimum). •	Comply with all current legislation, Building Regulations and Health & Safety requirements. Tender Submission Requirements Tender submissions shall include, along with the completed section at the end of this document: 1. Completed pricing schedule. 2. Proposed specification for hot water system replacement. 3. Project programme and estimated completion period. 4. Details of relevant experience on similar projects. 5. References for at least two comparable projects completed within the last five years. 6. Insurance certificates. 7. Health and Safety Policy. 8. Risk assessment / method statement for the works. 9. Confirmation that a copy of minor works certificate for electrical alterations would be available upon completion of works. Site Visits Tenderers are strongly encouraged to undertake a site visit before submitting their tender. Appointments should be arranged through the Parish Council. Budget The project is supported by: •	£20,000 Pride in Place grant •	Additional Parish Council budget allocation for 2027/28 The Council seeks best value and reserves the right to reject tenders that exceed available funding unless exceptional justification is provided. Tender Return Tenders must be submitted in a sealed envelope marked: "Tender - Trawden Recreation Ground Pavilion Refurbishment" to: Adele Smith, Parish Council Clerk, Trawden Forest Parish Council, C/O Trawden Community Library and Shop, Church Street, Trawden, Colne, Lancs BB8 8RU and received by the Parish Council no later than Friday 18th December 2026. All tenders received will be opened in line with the Council's financial regulations on a specific date with at least one Councillor present with the Clerk. Tenders received by any method other than sealed envelope delivery will be discarded. tender.title: Landscape Evidence Review and Spatial Strategy Support Study
tender.description:
Fareham Borough Council is preparing a new Local Plan to replace the adopted Fareham Local Plan 2037.
The Council has an extensive landscape evidence base which was prepared incrementally to support previous stages of plan-making.
The Council wishes to commission an independent specialist landscape consultancy to review the robustness, relevance and current policy alignment of this evidence base and advise whether it remains fit for purpose to support the preparation, examination and implementation of a new Local Plan.
The commission should consider the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) 2026, including the increased emphasis on landscape character, landscape-led planning, multifunctional green infrastructure, climate resilience and nature recovery.
The Council is seeking a proportionate review of existing evidence and does not currently intend to commission a completely new Landscape Character Assessment.

tender.title: Highway Structures - Confined space, roped access & difficult access inspections 2026
tender.description:
The North and Mid Wales Trunk Road Agent (NMWTRA) intends to procure services to undertake Principal Inspections of highway structures located throughout North and Mid Wales.
NMWTRA is seeking expressions of interest from organisations with proven experience in undertaking Principal Inspections in accordance with the Design Manual for Roads and Bridges (DMRB), including compliance with CS 450 and Welsh Government Structures Maintenance Manual. Tenderers will be required to provide inspection personnel holding current Bridge Inspector Certification Scheme (BICS) accreditation appropriate to the structures being inspected. Certain structures may require personnel holding Senior Bridge Inspector accreditation together with specialist access competencies relevant to the inspection activity.
The successful Contractor will be expected to provide all resources necessary to safely undertake the inspections, including specialist access equipment, qualified personnel, inspection planning, welfare facilities, and inspection reporting.
The contract is intended to establish a long-term relationship with a competent supplier capable of delivering a consistent programme of specialist-access Principal Inspections across the North and Mid Wales trunk road network throughout the four-year contract period.
The four-year contract period is anticipated to include approximately 60 Principal Inspections per annum. The structures portfolio comprises a diverse range of assets including highway bridges, retaining walls, culverts and other highway-related structures. Inspection locations will be distributed across the North and Mid Wales trunk road network.
A significant feature of this contract is that the inspection programme will comprise predominantly specialist-access inspections. Suppliers should anticipate the requirement to undertake inspections involving confined spaces, rope access techniques, work at height, work in or over water and other structures where specialist access methods are necessary to achieve the inspection requirements.
Please note that the value stated in this notice is an estimate based on a four-year period and is subject to funding availability and other relevant factors.

The Council of the Borough of Kirklees (the "Council") is conducting this procurement process using the competitive flexible procedure in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 ("the Act").
The Council wishes to establish a Framework of several Service Providers for the provision of Electrical Works and Goods. The Council intends to divide the Framework into Six Lots, including:
1) Full Rewires, additional and single item works to Domestic Properties (high volume)
2) Full Rewires, additional and single item works to Domestic Properties (low volume)
3) Domestic - Electrical Installation Condition Reports (EICR)
4) Contractor Switches
5) Electrical Materials
6) Mechanical Materials
It is anticipated the Framework will run for two (2) years with one (1) possible 24-month extension period.
Two previous notices have been published in relation to this Framework; UK1 and UK2. The OCID Reference is: ocds-h6vhtk-069fbf.

frameworkAgreement.description:
The Framework will operate through a combination of ranked direct award and competitive selection procedures. 
Upto 3 Suppliers will be appointed to Lots 1, 2, 3 and 4. 
Upto 5 Suppliers will be appointed to Lots 5 and 6. 
For Lots 1 to 4, suppliers will be ranked following evaluation and call-off contracts will normally be awarded sequentially to the highest-ranked supplier with sufficient capacity, capability and performance. 
Where a supplier is unable to meet the requirement, the opportunity will be offered to the next ranked supplier. 
For Lot 1 requirements exceeding £2.1 million, and where considered beneficial to secure improved value, innovation or risk management, a competitive selection process may be undertaken between all appointed suppliers on the Lot. 
For Lots 5 and 6, orders will be placed with the supplier offering the most advantageous arrangement at the point of purchase, taking account of price, discounts, availability, lead times and delivery requirements. 
Appropriate records will be maintained to ensure transparency and auditability.

tender.title: Procurement for LOLER Thorough Examination and Inspection Services (Habinteg)
tender.description:
Habinteg Housing Association invites tender responses for the provision of LOLER Thorough Examination and Inspection Services across its housing stock.
The successful Supplier will be responsible for providing an independent, competent and impartial inspection service and shall work collaboratively with Habinteg and any appointed lift maintenance contractors to ensure compliance risks are effectively managed and communicated.
The procurement of a LOLER Thorough Examination and Inspection Services provider is a key step in ensuring Habinteg continues to maintain safe and compliant lifting equipment, meets its statutory obligations, and provides assurance to residents and colleagues.
The successful Supplier will provide a comprehensive end-to-end compliance management service, including examination scheduling, inspection delivery, defect reporting, certification management, compliance tracking and management information reporting.

tender.title: Castell Conwy Interpretation Project
tender.description:
Cadw is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified and experienced Interpretation Consultant to support a programme of new interpretation at Castell Conwy, north Wales. This will include researching and preparing an interpretation plan for Castell Conwy which will inform a suite of costed options for the design, fabrication, installation and ongoing maintenance of new interpretive media (considered to be RIBA stage 0/1 and then developed to RIBA stage 2). It is envisaged the interpretation will need to be procured alongside any required conservation building work at the monument.  The building work will be procured and led by Cadw’s Project Management Team.
As noted elsewhere in this notice (and accompanying tender documentation), the appointment of the successful contractor will be via a two-stage Competitive Flexible Procedure under the provisions of the Procurement Act 2023.  Stage 1 will consist of a qualification stage to assess bidder's capability and past experience in delivering complex high value interpretation projects at historically significant monuments.  Shortlisted bidders will then be invited to stage 2 where outline designs can be presented for evaluation.
The values included in this notice are further explained in the accompanying tender documentation and could be subject to increase.  The total included in the notice is for the design and fabrication/installation of all interpretation at Castell Conwy.  For clarity, this total value is split between £100,000 to £180,000 for the design element and £500,000 to  £800,000 for the fabrication/installation of the full interpretation scheme.  There is the possibility that the total value could increase to up to £2,000,000 for design and fabrication/installation but this upper limit is subject to additional approvals and budget availability.  Interested bidders should work to the £980,000 total when formulating their bid.

procedure.features: The appointment of the successful contractor will be via a two-stage Competitive Flexible Procedure under the provisions of the Procurement Act 2023.  The two-stage procurement route will include a qualification stage to assess bidder’s capability and past experience in delivering complex high value interpretation projects at historically significant monuments.  Shortlisted bidder’s will then be invited to Stage 2 where outline design ideas can be presented along with associated costs.  Further particulars of the process to be used are noted in the accompanying stage 1 and stage 2 tender documentation included in the etender portal and attached to this notice.  Bidders should note that the stage 2 documentation included is in draft format and may therefore change prior to the commencement of stage 2.  Any changes will be noted to shortlisted bidders.
